<reason>B more convincingly separated harmful amplification from political subject matter. Its discovery objection survived throughout: an easy toggle does not supply the missing introduction that would motivate opting in. A developed a meaningful verification advantage, but never showed why easier enforcement outweighed excluding useful civic discovery, or why retaining some engagement signal necessarily preserved radicalization. B answered pressure directly and sharpened the comparison; A increasingly relied on unsupported inevitability claims.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B decisively turned A’s worker-video concession against it: a grievance can be furious while a proposal for legal reform can be calm. This exposed the mismatch between A’s stated target—outrage-driven amplification—and its actual trigger—political subject matter—even if the rule were perfectly enforceable.</best_rebuttal>
